video_title: Lakers Q&A: Is One More Move Coming? Kuminga Interest, Asking Price & More

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers remain interested in Jonathan Kuminga despite recent roster moves
quotes.excerpt: They remain on Jonathan Kuminga watch. This is I guess we're a week into it.
quotes.quote: They remain on Jonathan Kuminga watch. This is I guess we're a week into it. It's day seven, day eight of Kuminga watch basically since the Lakers did their first flurry of moves. Technically the Lakers can still create cap space and sign Jonathan Kuminga up until they do the Sexton and Reeves moves because once they do the Sexton move, they will be using the room exception and then the Austin move fully puts them above the cap where it's really difficult at that point to create any cap space.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaden Hardy remains a trade candidate for the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: Hardy can still be aggregated in a trade because he was acquired with cap space.
quotes.quote: Hardy can still be aggregated in a trade because he was acquired with cap space. So there's been a lot of misinformation out there in terms of Jaden Hardy can't be traded or Jaden Hardy can't be aggregated in a trade. Because the Lakers acquired him using cap space, they can still reroute Jaden Hardy immediately. There's no 60-day period with him. So they can trade him right now. They can trade him tomorrow.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Atlanta is open to trading Jonathan Kuminga to the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: Atlanta is open to trading Jonathan Kuminga to the Lakers in a sign-and-trade.
quotes.quote: Atlanta is open to trading Jonathan Kuminga to the Lakers in a sign-and-trade with the framework being Jared Vanderbilt and the Lakers 2032 first-round swap. Now I have heard the Lakers are reluctant to give up that swap and are reluctant to give up that swap in that specific deal. I'm on the side of I think if you can get off Jared Vanderbilt for just a first-round swap and retain those three second-round picks and get a starting-level forward back, that to me is a no-brainer.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers trade rules and salary matching constraints explained
quotes.excerpt: If the Lakers are sending out anything in the 8.8 million dollar range or below, they can take back double.
quotes.quote: If the Lakers are sending out anything in the 8.8 million dollar range or below, they can take back double the salary plus 250,000 dollars. For example, Jaden Hardy is on a 6 million dollar contract. If the Lakers send out just Jaden Hardy, they get to take back a player making up to 12.25 million, which would be double his salary plus that 250,000 dollars. If the player is making between 8.8 million and 29 million, they can add up to 9.1 million on top of that. For example, Jared Vanderbilt making 12.4 million, if you send out Vando, you can roughly bring back 21.5 million in a trade.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Jovan Buha disagrees with the assessment of PJ Washington's contract
quotes.excerpt: I also vehemently disagree with that assessment from the Lakers' perspective.
quotes.quote: I also vehemently disagree with that assessment from the Lakers' perspective just because PJ Washington is better than Quentin Grimes and Mamu. And he's also fitting this timeline of the Luka, Austin, and younger group of he's 27. He's about to be 28 in August, so he's a little bit on the older side. He'd be the second oldest rotation guy or second oldest starter behind just Austin. PJ Washington is on the timeline. He's locked up for four years, so he also fits with you're trying to get everyone on the same timeline in terms of the contracts.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Jonathan Kuminga's potential fit and contract risk for the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: Unless he's ready to buy in to being a super role player like Andrew Wiggins/Mikal Bridges I don't wanna give up assets for a new DLo
quotes.quote: I get the pros for JK but doesn't he see himself as 'The Guy.' Unless he's ready to buy in to being a super role player like Andrew Wiggins/Mikal Bridges I don't wanna give up assets for a new DLo. Kuminga, it's a little bit more risk. If you're signing a three-year deal, potentially 15 million range or even maybe higher, there's some risk in that. It's a different calculation and I don't have the answer. If I knew he was going to fully buy in, I'd be pushing even harder for it. If I knew he wasn't, I'd obviously be completely off of it, but we don't know.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Walker Kessler as a stretch big for the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: I'd actually argue that the stretch big archetype is really important against contenders
quotes.quote: I like this idea. I would say that you could do both against both. I'd actually argue that the stretch big archetype is really important against contenders and that against the crappier teams, for lack of a better word, that's where he could feast on the inside. Take a step back here, think about when Deandre Ayton and Jackson Hayes would look like prime Dwight Howard or DeAndre Jordan or Tyson Chandler. It would be when they were playing the worst teams in the league and they were playing the Brooklyns, the New Orleans, the Washingtons. Those guys would feast and have their seven-for-seven shooting nights where it's five dunks and two putbacks or two dump-offs or whatever. Those guys look like All-Stars and superheroes against the worst defenses in the league because of how bad they were defensively and how easily Luka and Austin were able to get downhill in the pick-and-roll and then set them up for lobs and easy baskets. So I would actually almost flip this. I like the big Walker versus the weaker teams and I like the stretch Walker against the better teams because what you're going to want to do is stretch Victor Wembanyama, bring him out from the paint. What you're going to want to do is test Kessler's ability to rotate and in closeout to Kessler and then make the second rotation down to be the low man. What you're going to want is to space out the Thunder and get one of Hartenstein or Chet out of the paint.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' trade options if they miss on Jonathan Kuminga
quotes.excerpt: It's one of two pathways. One is enticing and one is the pressing.
quotes.quote: It would be the rest of the trade. It's one of two pathways. One is enticing and one is the pressing. The enticing one is you still explore the trade market: the PJ Washington, Derrick Jones Jr., Lou Dort, Christian Brown, Cam Johnson, Max Strus, Max Strus, someone like that. You go that route of the guys making somewhere between 10 to 20 million. Everyone there is between 10 and a half and 23 million. So you explore that. Or you take a couple swings on the minimum market and I just think that if you have this glaring hole in your starting group and you're hoping to plug it with a minimum player, I think that's a mistake and I just don't think it's going to work. I could be wrong, it happens, but just look at the Knicks are basically starting five plus 20 million dollar guys and then the Spurs and Thunder, the guys that they were starting that were cheap were guys on rookie scale contracts that were like lottery picks. It's just there's no, I guess, Champagnie is maybe the closest analog here. Like if you find your Julian Champagnie, okay, that's the exception. That's about it.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Clarifying the Los Angeles Lakers' actual NBA draft pick flexibility
quotes.excerpt: They have three of their next seven picks, but two of them have been pick swapped
quotes.quote: I think as I laid out at the top, they have a little bit more flexibility than people are indicating, but certainly they don't have all this flexibility or all this optionality. It is limited. They're limited in terms of what they can trade. That's the biggest thing. I think the point I was more so trying to make was like, I think when people make that point, they're like, oh, the Lakers don't have any of their picks for the next seven years. That's just not true. They have three of their next seven picks, but two of them have been pick swapped and one of them they might pick swap. So that's more so the point, the clarification I'm trying to make.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic's influence and accountability regarding the Dallas Mavericks roster
quotes.excerpt: Luka has signed off on this roster to a degree.
quotes.quote: I mean, I think one of the things that has sort of been trickling out there and is now out there in multiple forms of reporting is like, Luka has signed off on this roster to a degree. So I think this will be another situation, kind of similar to what we had at times in the LeBron era, where it's like, okay, if the roster doesn't pan out and you're not happy with it, well, you were complicit in the roster looking the way it was and you didn't push back on the Gabe Vincent signing or Torian Prince, whatever. I don't think it's as black and white as that, but like, I think there would be a little bit of pushback from the Lakers of like, we got you the center, we moved heaven and earth to get that for you. We got you your buddies in Grimes and Hardy. We got you more shooting and dynamism offensively. We tried to do everything we could in our power to give you what you wanted.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' front office and roster construction philosophy
quotes.excerpt: I feel like they sometimes overreact or overcorrect and you'll see the genesis of most of the mess the Lakers have been in
quotes.quote: It's one of the things I think the Lakers, I would say one of the flaws or one of the weaknesses of the front office in my opinion over the last few years has been, I feel like they sometimes overreact or overcorrect and you'll see the genesis of most of the mess the Lakers have been in has been dating back to the title team on paper not having like a certain level of offense or a certain level of ball handling or whatever. And then they started trying to make up for that first with the Dennis Schroder trade which became an utter disaster where they gave up the pick of Jaden McDaniels with Danny Green for Schroder when like you had Jaden McDaniels sitting there. Obviously you didn't know he was going to be that, but like that ended up being a very costly trade that they clearly lost. And then from that point on, you pursue a third star that summer. You're going after Dame, you're going after Bradley Beal, you're going after DeMar DeRozan, you end up settling on Russell Westbrook. And then from that point on, I think the Lakers have been, it's been, okay, we have too much roster turnover. Then after 2023, let's resign everybody. Let's extend Rui, let's extend Vando, let's resign DLo, and it's like, well we need to give this group some runway here. So let's basically not make any moves in 2024 either or make minor moves, Gabe Vincent, Torian Prince, whatever.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' rotation and need for more depth
quotes.excerpt: I see six currently. I would say seven if they get Kuminga or PJ.
quotes.quote: I see six currently. I would say seven if they get Kuminga or PJ. There's like two wildcards. Maybe three. I mean I think it do technically a wildcard but with how his Summer League has gone so far, he might be a wild wildcard and we'll see how the rest of the summer goes. But I look at Cameron Carr and Jake LaRavia as two guys who have potential to extend this to eight or nine, depending on how that goes with each of them. Cameron Carr obviously been really impressed with him to start Summer League and just the off-ball utility as a coming off of screens, as a pick-and-roll guy, as a cutter, getting out in transition, like just, you know, mainly the off-ball stuff because I think that's going to be his primary usage. And that's another guy, I didn't even mention him compared to Hardy, he'd be ahead of Hardy too, in my opinion. I think Carr has the potential, and then Jake if he regains his shot, I think has the utility with the defense and the rebounding, but those are ifs. We don't know that for sure and to count on a rookie in a playoff series is possible, but it's often like the lottery, you know, like there's a reason why Dylan Harper's performance was so special and not that Carr is going to be held to the Dylan Harper standard, but in general, rookies, it's more like the Carter Bryant where you're trying to fit them in to a rotation, but they kind of look like they're playing deer in the headlights basketball.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Austin Reaves contract value and Lakers' roster retention strategy
quotes.excerpt: I think at least the first couple years are in line with his current production/value.
quotes.quote: On Austin Reaves, I think at least the first couple years are in line with his current production and value. I think for him to hit on years three and four, he does have to continue to level up and at least play closer to the level he was at the first month or two months of the season. But with Austin Reaves, I think they could not lose that asset. So once he was getting max offers from other teams, they felt they had to pay him. It was more than I thought he was going to make, it was more than a lot of fans thought he was going to make, but they could not lose him.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' roster construction issues regarding size and playoff experience
quotes.excerpt: The Lakers continue to add small guards and even Quentin Grimes in a point of attack role.
quotes.quote: The Lakers continue to add small guards and even Quentin Grimes, in a point of attack role, I think that's fine, but in a wing stopper role which is currently slotted to play with the current group, I guess unless they're slotting Mamadi Diakite at the starting four. The funny thing is, two of those guys have not even played in the playoffs in Walker Kessler and Collin Sexton. Mamadi Diakite played in the playoffs in one series and was bad this past postseason. Quentin Grimes has played in the playoffs twice and I think was kind of shaky this postseason as well.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Rob Pelinka needs to improve the Lakers' negotiating position
quotes.excerpt: Rob needs to get himself some optionality. With limited assets, our moves become telegraphed and puts us in poor negotiating position.
quotes.quote: Rob needs to get himself some optionality. With limited assets, our moves become telegraphed and puts us in poor negotiating position. Need options to be able to pivot in future, avoid tunnel vision.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' limited assets and obvious needs hurt their trade leverage
quotes.excerpt: One of the bigger issues for the Lakers the last two years is they have had such limited assets and such obvious needs.
quotes.quote: One of the bigger issues for the Lakers the last two years is they have had such limited assets and such obvious needs, where they go into every negotiation in my opinion, or most, at a deficit. It's pretty obvious what they need. They need a center or they need a 3-D wing. Now they got the center spot handled, but it's like, if the Lakers are calling you, they're clearly looking for a starting forward or some sort of defensive wing. Based on clear roster needs and a limited amount of assets, teams can then demand the moon from them, and that's why sometimes the Lakers' price on the market ends up being a bit higher than the typical market price.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Jonathan Kuminga's potential trade value and contract concerns
quotes.excerpt: The risk with Kuminga is you just don't know how bought in he's going to be.
quotes.quote: The risk with Kuminga is you just don't know how bought in he's going to be. You don't know if he's going to have that mercenary mindset of ball out on the Lakers stage, get the spotlight, the audience, the attention, and then go cash out somewhere else. That's a possibility. But for the Lakers, if he does ball out, if he does buy in, you obviously benefit from that too in terms of at least while he's on your roster, that level of play.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Rob Pelinka's job security and the Walker Kessler trade
quotes.excerpt: If you want to criticize the Walker Kessler move, I don't think it's the assets or the contract, I think it's how much you gave up for him on the trade market.
quotes.quote: If you want to criticize the Walker Kessler move, I don't think it's the assets or the contract, I think it's how much you gave up for him on the trade market. That was obviously a leverage thing with Utah, and they knew how much the Lakers wanted Kessler, how perfect of a fit he'd be, how much Luka wanted that. To me, if anything, that comes off as more of a desperate attempt to save your job than a GM who just doesn't care about his job and is just like, I'm just going to make these moves and see how it plays out.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Evaluating the potential fit of DJJ versus Daniel Gafford
quotes.excerpt: I would really like DJJ for slotting Grimes in a six-man role and balancing out with Kuminga and DJJ.
quotes.quote: I would really like DJJ for slotting Grimes in a six-man role and balancing out with Kuminga and DJJ. I just really like that three-four offensive combination. Obviously defensively, it's going to be Luka as the three-four, Kuminga as the three-four opposite Luka, and then DJJ more as a backcourt guy with Austin. But I think I would lean DJJ. What I like about Gafford is then it gives you a high-level backup and I feel really good about the center spot. If Kessler goes down, Gafford slots in as the starting five and you have like real insurance there in a way that I don't think you currently have.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaden Hardy's defensive limitations and trade value
quotes.excerpt: Hardy is statistically one of the worst defenders in the league. He's also a pretty bad finisher at the rim.
quotes.quote: Hardy is statistically one of the worst defenders in the league. He's also a pretty bad finisher at the rim. His primary utility is actually as a shooter, which I guess you could say, hey, catch and shoot, spot up, just be an off-ball shooter, okay, maybe he's willing to play that, although he is a guy who likes the ball at his hands. He's more of a ball handler, but the defense is bad and it makes, if you have concerns with Sexton or Austin or whatever, like he makes those guys look like all-defense type guys, at least statistically.
